Maaleh-acrabbim
MAH-uh-leh-uh-KRAB-im
proper noun
Hebrew Maaleh Aqrabbim, “the ascent of scorpions” (also the ascent of Akrabbim); a steep pass on the southern border of Judah and of the promised land.

Biblical Definition

Maaleh-acrabbim, “the ascent of scorpions,” was a steep and rugged pass marking the southern border of Judah and of the whole land: “And it went out to the south side to Maalehacrabbim, and passed along to Zin” (Josh 15:3); and again in the tracing of the national boundary, “your border shall turn from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim” (Num 34:4). It was a hard climb through country infested with scorpions, a fitting emblem of the toil and danger by which the border of the promise was reached. The wilderness through which Israel passed was “that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions,” and yet the LORD led His people through it and brought them up. The ascent of scorpions preaches that the way into the inheritance is upward and beset with dangers, but that God is faithful to bring His people through. So the Christian’s path to the heavenly Canaan is steep and thronged with enemies, yet the Lord has given His own authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt them. The scorpion-pass is climbed, and the promised land lies beyond.

Webster 1828 Definition

“The ascent of scorpions,” a steep pass on the southern border of Judah and the land (Josh 15:3; Num 34:4); an emblem of the hard, upward, serpent-beset way into the inheritance.

MAALEH-ACRABBIM, “the ascent of scorpions,” a pass on Judah’s southern border.

Named in the border-line of Judah (Josh 15:3).

Also the border of the whole land (Num 34:4).

A steep climb through scorpion-infested country.

An emblem of the hard, upward way into the inheritance.

Key Scripture

Josh 15:3 — "And it went out to the south side to Maalehacrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and ascended up on the south side unto Kadeshbarnea, and passed along to Hezron, and went up to Adar, and fetched a compass to Karkaa: Maalehacrebbim: or, the going up to Acrabbim"

Num 34:4 — "And your border shall turn from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass on to Zin: and the going forth thereof shall be from the south to Kadeshbarnea, and shall go on to Hazaraddar, and pass on to Azmon:"

Deu 32:8 — "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

Josh 21:45 — "There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass."

Modern Corruption

A steep border-pass, “the ascent of scorpions”; it recovers the truth that the way into the inheritance is hard and serpent-beset, yet God brings His people through.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A rugged desert pass raises no modern controversy. Its vivid name, “ascent of scorpions,” carries its own sermon: the border of the promise is reached by a hard and dangerous climb.

The principle to recover is that the way into God’s inheritance is upward and beset with danger, but that He is faithful to bring His people through. Israel crossed a wilderness of fiery serpents and scorpions, yet the LORD led her up. The Lord Jesus gives His own authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy; the Christian’s steep and thorny road ends in the promised rest, for none shall pluck His people out of His hand.
